title: Fact or opinion?
goal: Tell facts from opinions in news texts by spotting evaluative words, modalizers and the journalistic conditional, and present information neutrally yourself.

items.fr: le conditionnel journalistique : la Ville aurait décidé…
items.en: the journalistic conditional (unconfirmed information: reportedly, allegedly)

drills.text: Selon nos sources, la Ville ___ vendre le bâtiment. (envisager)
drills.en: According to our sources, the City is reportedly considering selling the building.

drills.text: Le maire ___ ___ le rapport dès janvier. (recevoir, past)
drills.en: The mayor allegedly received the report as early as January.
drills.explain: Unconfirmed past fact → conditionnel passé: [[aurait reçu]].

drills.prompt: What does “L'incendie aurait fait trois blessés” mean?
options: The fire reportedly injured three people (not confirmed).
The fire would have injured three people if…
The fire injured three people (confirmed).
The fire will injure three people.
drills.explain: In news, the conditional signals information the journalist has not confirmed.

items.en: modalizers: words that reveal the writer's attitude

drills.prompt: Which sentence contains the writer's opinion?
options: Malheureusement, la Ville a choisi la solution la plus facile.
La Ville a voté la fermeture lundi soir.
Le bâtiment a été construit en 1972.
La bibliothèque compte deux employés.
drills.explain: [[Malheureusement]] and [[la solution la plus facile]] are judgments; the others can be checked.

drills.text: Le projet sera ___ ___ adopté : la majorité des conseillers le soutient.
drills.en: The project will probably be adopted: most councillors support it.
drills.explain: [[sans doute]] = probably (not “without doubt”, which is [[sans aucun doute]]).

items.note: In the singular the t is usually pronounced: [fɛt] (you may also hear [fɛ]). Plural des faits: [fɛ].
The writer is un chroniqueur / une chroniqueuse.

items.en: news wire story, short factual news report

steps.title: One event, two texts
steps.intro: Read both texts about the same event. The first one **reports**; the second one **comments**. As you read, mark each sentence **F** (fact) or **O** (opinion).

blocks.title: Text 1. News report: the Bellerive branch library will close
blocks.context: An original, fictional news report on a regional news site.
blocks.fr:
Le conseil municipal de Saint-Aurèle a voté lundi soir la fermeture de la bibliothèque du quartier Bellerive, à compter du 1er juillet. La décision a été adoptée par sept voix contre deux.
Selon la Ville, la fermeture permettra d'économiser environ 400 000 $ par année. Le bâtiment, construit en 1972, nécessite d'importants travaux de toiture. Les collections seront transférées à la bibliothèque centrale, située à quatre kilomètres.
Selon nos informations, la Ville envisagerait de vendre le terrain à un promoteur immobilier. Le cabinet de la mairesse n'a pas confirmé cette information.
Une pétition contre la fermeture a recueilli près de 3 000 signatures, d'après le comité de citoyens qui l'a lancée. Une quarantaine de résidents ont assisté à la séance.
blocks.en: Saint-Aurèle city council voted on Monday evening to close the library in the Bellerive neighbourhood, as of July 1. The decision was adopted by seven votes to two. According to the City, the closure will save about $400,000 a year. The building, built in 1972, needs major roof work. The collections will be transferred to the central library, four kilometres away. According to our information, the City is reportedly considering selling the land to a property developer. The mayor's office did not confirm this information. A petition against the closure has collected nearly 3,000 signatures, according to the citizens' committee that launched it. About forty residents attended the meeting.

blocks.title: Text 2. Column: “Closing a library is closing a door”
blocks.context: An original, fictional opinion column by Camille Ouellet in the same news site.
blocks.fr:
Lundi soir, le conseil municipal a pris une décision franchement regrettable. En fermant la bibliothèque de Bellerive, la Ville a choisi la solution la plus facile, comme d'habitude.
Certes, 400 000 $, ce n'est pas rien. Mais une bibliothèque de quartier, c'est bien plus qu'un bâtiment avec une toiture qui coule. C'est l'endroit où les enfants font leurs devoirs, où les aînés lisent le journal, où les nouveaux arrivants trouvent des cours de conversation gratuits. Pour beaucoup de familles, la bibliothèque centrale, à quatre kilomètres, est tout simplement inaccessible.
On nous parle d'économies. Visiblement, personne à l'hôtel de ville n'a calculé ce que coûtera l'isolement de tout un quartier. Et si, comme le prétendent certains, le terrain finit entre les mains d'un promoteur, la prétendue « contrainte budgétaire » aura bon dos.
La mairesse aime répéter que sa ville est « inclusive ». Elle a malheureusement manqué une belle occasion de le prouver.
blocks.en: On Monday evening, city council made a frankly regrettable decision. By closing the Bellerive library, the City chose the easiest solution, as usual. Admittedly, $400,000 is not nothing. But a neighbourhood library is much more than a building with a leaking roof. It's the place where children do their homework, where seniors read the paper, where newcomers find free conversation classes. For many families, the central library, four kilometres away, is simply out of reach. We're told about savings. Clearly, nobody at city hall calculated what the isolation of an entire neighbourhood will cost. And if, as some claim, the land ends up in a developer's hands, the so-called “budget constraint” will turn out to be a convenient excuse. The mayor likes to repeat that her city is “inclusive”. Unfortunately, she missed a fine opportunity to prove it.

blocks.prompt: In Text 1, why is “la Ville envisagerait de vendre le terrain” in the conditional?
options: The information is not confirmed.
It is a polite request.
It is a hypothesis with si.
It is the writer's opinion.
blocks.explain: [[Selon nos informations…]] + conditional, and [[Le cabinet… n'a pas confirmé]]: the journalist signals that it is unconfirmed.

blocks.prompt: Which sentence from Text 2 is a fact that can be checked?
options: La bibliothèque centrale est à quatre kilomètres.
Le conseil a pris une décision franchement regrettable.
La Ville a choisi la solution la plus facile, comme d'habitude.
Elle a malheureusement manqué une belle occasion.
blocks.explain: A distance is verifiable. [[regrettable]], [[la plus facile]], [[comme d'habitude]], [[malheureusement]] are judgments.

blocks.title: Fact or opinion: the clues
head: Clue
Fact (information)
Opinion (comment)
rows: time and place: lundi, à quatre kilomètres
selon la Ville, d'après le comité
the writer's voice: on nous parle de…
irony, quotation marks: la prétendue « contrainte »
blocks.note: Careful: a text can mix both. A column contains facts too (400 000 $, quatre kilomètres); a news report can hide an opinion in one adjective.

blocks.title: Words for talking about the media
The journalistic conditional
blocks.pattern: conditionnel présent (now) / conditionnel passé (past) = information not confirmed
blocks.note: Journalists use the conditional to report something **without taking responsibility for it**. In English you'd add *reportedly*, *allegedly*, *is said to*. It is often paired with a source: [[selon nos informations]], [[selon des témoins]], [[de source sûre]].

examples.fr: Le ministre démissionnerait dans les prochains jours.
examples.en: The minister is reportedly going to resign in the coming days.

examples.fr: Selon des témoins, le conducteur aurait brûlé un feu rouge.
examples.en: According to witnesses, the driver allegedly ran a red light.

examples.fr: L'entreprise aurait supprimé une centaine de postes.
examples.en: The company is said to have cut about a hundred jobs.

blocks.title: Modalizers: the writer's fingerprints
blocks.body:
**Modalizers** are words that show the writer's attitude. Spot them and you find the opinion.

- **Certainty / probability:** [[sans doute]] (probably), [[certainement]], [[peut-être]], [[visiblement]] (clearly, apparently)
- **Feeling:** [[heureusement]], [[malheureusement]], [[hélas]] (alas)
- **Distance:** [[prétendu]] (so-called), [[soi-disant]] (supposedly), quotation marks around a word
- **Evaluative adjectives:** [[regrettable]], [[remarquable]], [[inquiétant]], [[absurde]]
- **Verbs of opinion:** [[il semble que]], [[on peut craindre que]], [[force est de constater que]] (one has to admit that)

examples.fr: La prétendue réforme ne change rien.
Visiblement, personne n'a lu le rapport.

blocks.body:
- **sans doute ≠ without a doubt:** [[sans doute]] means *probably*. *Without a doubt* is [[sans aucun doute]].
- **Conditional = opinion?** No: the journalistic conditional marks **uncertainty**, not the writer's judgment.
- **Numbers = facts?** A number is verifiable, but who gives it matters: [[selon la Ville, 400 000 $]] is the City's figure, not necessarily the truth.
- **éditorial vs chronique:** an [[éditorial]] speaks for the newspaper; a [[chronique]] is one columnist's personal view.

In Québec media you'll often read [[le cabinet de la mairesse / du ministre]] (the mayor's / minister's office), [[l'hôtel de ville]] (city hall) and [[la séance du conseil]] (council meeting). [[Mairesse]] is the usual feminine of [[maire]] in Québec; in France, [[la maire]] is now common too. Columnists are very popular in Québec: many newspapers publish several [[chroniques]] every day, next to news reports.

blocks.title: Listen and repeat
blocks.note: News anchors read the conditional with a neutral tone. Columnists stress their evaluative words.

lines.fr: Selon nos informations, la Ville envisagerait de vendre le terrain.
lines.en: According to our information, the City is reportedly considering selling the land.

lines.fr: Le maire aurait reçu le rapport en janvier.
lines.en: The mayor allegedly received the report in January.

lines.fr: Le conseil a pris une décision franchement regrettable.
lines.en: The council made a frankly regrettable decision.
lines.tip: Stress franchement regrettable: that's the opinion.

blocks.fr: Selon des témoins, le camion aurait roulé trop vite.
blocks.en: According to witnesses, the truck was allegedly going too fast.
blocks.prompt: Is the speed of the truck confirmed?
options: No, it's what witnesses say.
Yes, the police confirmed it.
Yes, the journalist saw it.
No, the truck was stopped.
blocks.explain: [[Selon des témoins]] + [[aurait roulé]] (conditionnel passé): not confirmed.

blocks.fr: Visiblement, la mairesse n'a pas écouté les résidents.
blocks.en: Clearly, the mayor didn't listen to residents.
blocks.prompt: What kind of sentence is this?
options: An opinion
A verifiable fact
An unconfirmed rumour
A quotation
blocks.explain: [[Visiblement]] is a modalizer: the speaker interprets the mayor's behaviour.

steps.title: Your turn
steps.intro: Some items bring back unit 3 (impersonal structures, nuance).

options: La décision a été adoptée par sept voix contre deux.
La décision est profondément injuste.
La Ville a encore une fois oublié les familles.
C'est une belle victoire pour les citoyens.
blocks.explain: A vote result can be checked; the others contain judgments ([[injuste]], [[oublié]], [[belle victoire]]).

blocks.text: Selon des témoins, le suspect se ___ ___ par la fenêtre. (s'enfuir, past)
blocks.en: According to witnesses, the suspect allegedly escaped through the window.
blocks.explain: Unconfirmed past fact → conditionnel passé. [[s'enfuir]] takes être: [[se serait enfui]].

blocks.prompt: Match the genre with its description.
pairs: a reader's or citizen's public letter

blocks.prompt: The company is reportedly going to close two factories.
accept: L'entreprise s'apprêterait à fermer deux usines.
Selon nos informations, l'entreprise fermerait deux usines.
Selon nos sources, l'entreprise fermerait deux usines.
L'entreprise s'apprêterait à fermer deux de ses usines.
blocks.hint: No need for “reportedly”: the conditional says it.
blocks.explain: The journalistic conditional [[fermerait]] = is reportedly going to close.

blocks.text: Il viendra sans ___ ___ à la réunion : il a confirmé hier.
blocks.en: He will come to the meeting without a doubt: he confirmed yesterday.
blocks.explain: Certainty → [[sans aucun doute]]. Plain [[sans doute]] would only mean *probably*.

blocks.prompt: In “la prétendue contrainte budgétaire”, what does the writer suggest?
options: The budget constraint is not the real reason.
The budget constraint is very serious.
The budget constraint was officially confirmed.
There is no budget at all.
blocks.explain: [[prétendu]] (so-called) shows distance: the writer doesn't believe the official reason.

blocks.prompt: According to our information, the mayor is reportedly going to resign.
accept: Selon nos informations le maire démissionnerait
Le maire démissionnerait selon nos informations

blocks.text: Il est clair que le bâtiment ___ besoin de travaux, mais il n'est pas certain que la Ville ___ le rénover. (avoir, pouvoir)
blocks.en: It's clear that the building needs work, but it's not certain that the City can renovate it.
blocks.explain: Unit 3: certainty → indicative [[a]]; negated certainty = doubt → subjunctive [[puisse]].

blocks.fr: Le cabinet de la mairesse n'a pas confirmé cette information.
blocks.explain: [[mairesse]] (Québec feminine of maire); [[confirmé]] agrees with nothing here (avoir, no preceding object).

blocks.prompt: A friend sends you the column about the library. In about 90 seconds, explain the difference between the news report and the column: give two facts, two opinions, and say which text you trust more for information, and why.
checklist: Two opinions with the clue words (regrettable, malheureusement…)
Mention the conditional and what it means
Say which text is more reliable for facts, with a reason

models.label: Model answer
models.fr: Les deux textes parlent de la même décision, mais ils sont très différents. Le premier est un article d'information : il donne des faits, par exemple le vote, sept contre deux, et l'économie de 400 000 $ selon la Ville. Le deuxième est une chronique : la journaliste dit que la décision est « regrettable » et que la Ville a choisi la solution la plus facile. Ce sont des opinions. Dans le premier texte, la vente du terrain est au conditionnel, donc ce n'est pas confirmé. Pour m'informer, je fais plus confiance au premier texte, mais la chronique donne de bons arguments.
models.en: Both texts talk about the same decision, but they're very different. The first is a news article: it gives facts, for example the vote, seven to two, and the $400,000 saving according to the City. The second is a column: the journalist says the decision is “regrettable” and that the City chose the easiest solution. Those are opinions. In the first text, the sale of the land is in the conditional, so it's not confirmed. To get informed, I trust the first text more, but the column gives good arguments.

models.label: Stronger model answer
models.fr: Ces deux textes traitent du même événement, mais pas avec le même objectif. Le premier, une dépêche, informe : il rapporte des faits vérifiables, comme le résultat du vote, sept voix contre deux, ou la date de fermeture, le 1er juillet. Il cite aussi ses sources : le chiffre de 400 000 $ vient de la Ville, celui de la pétition vient du comité de citoyens. Quand l'information n'est pas confirmée, le journaliste utilise le conditionnel : la Ville « envisagerait » de vendre le terrain. Le second texte, une chronique, commente. Les jugements de valeur sont partout : « une décision franchement regrettable », « comme d'habitude », « malheureusement ». La chroniqueuse parle même de la « prétendue » contrainte budgétaire, ce qui montre qu'elle doute de la version officielle. Pour connaître les faits, je me fierais donc à la dépêche. Cela dit, la chronique a le mérite de poser une vraie question : ce que coûte l'isolement d'un quartier.
models.en: These two texts deal with the same event, but not with the same aim. The first, a news report, informs: it reports verifiable facts, such as the result of the vote, seven to two, or the closing date, July 1. It also cites its sources: the $400,000 figure comes from the City, the petition figure from the citizens' committee. When information isn't confirmed, the journalist uses the conditional: the City “is reportedly considering” selling the land. The second text, a column, comments. Value judgments are everywhere: “a frankly regrettable decision”, “as usual”, “unfortunately”. The columnist even speaks of the “so-called” budget constraint, which shows she doubts the official version. To know the facts, I would therefore rely on the news report. That said, the column has the merit of raising a real question: what the isolation of a neighbourhood costs.

blocks.prompt: Rewrite this biased paragraph as a neutral news report (80–120 words). Keep only verifiable facts, add sources, and use the conditional for anything unconfirmed: “Once again, our incompetent council has made a scandalous decision: it raised bus fares by 10% on Monday, while the service is worse than ever. Apparently, the mayor even wants to cut two lines, which would be a disaster for families.”
blocks.promptFr: Réécrivez ce paragraphe sous forme de dépêche neutre.
checklist: No evaluative adjectives or attitude adverbs
The conditional for the unconfirmed information
Third person, neutral verbs (a voté, a annoncé)

models.label: Model answer
models.fr: Le conseil municipal a voté lundi soir une hausse de 10 % des tarifs d'autobus. La mesure entrera en vigueur le 1er septembre. Selon la Ville, cette hausse est nécessaire pour financer l'entretien des véhicules. Plusieurs usagers se plaignent toutefois de retards fréquents sur le réseau. Selon nos informations, la mairesse envisagerait aussi de supprimer deux lignes d'autobus. Son cabinet n'a pas confirmé cette information. Un comité d'usagers a annoncé qu'il présenterait une pétition lors de la prochaine séance du conseil.
models.en: City council voted on Monday evening for a 10% increase in bus fares. The measure will come into force on September 1. According to the City, this increase is necessary to fund vehicle maintenance. Several riders, however, complain of frequent delays on the network. According to our information, the mayor is also reportedly considering cutting two bus lines. Her office did not confirm this information. A riders' committee announced that it would present a petition at the next council meeting.

models.label: Stronger model answer
models.fr: Saint-Aurèle. Le conseil municipal a adopté lundi soir une hausse de 10 % des tarifs du transport collectif, qui entrera en vigueur le 1er septembre. D'après l'administration, cette augmentation doit permettre de couvrir la hausse des coûts d'entretien. Selon l'Association des usagers, la ponctualité du réseau s'est pourtant dégradée depuis un an, une affirmation que la Ville conteste. Par ailleurs, la mairesse envisagerait de supprimer deux lignes jugées peu fréquentées, selon un document interne consulté par notre rédaction. Interrogé mardi, son cabinet n'a ni confirmé ni démenti cette information. La prochaine séance du conseil aura lieu le 14 octobre.
models.en: Saint-Aurèle. City council adopted on Monday evening a 10% increase in public transit fares, which will come into force on September 1. According to the administration, this increase should cover rising maintenance costs. According to the Riders' Association, however, the network's punctuality has deteriorated over the past year, a claim the City disputes. In addition, the mayor is reportedly considering cutting two lines deemed underused, according to an internal document seen by our newsroom. Asked on Tuesday, her office neither confirmed nor denied this information. The next council meeting will take place on October 14.

summary:
- Tell facts (verifiable, sourced) from opinions (evaluative adjectives, modalizers like [[malheureusement]], [[visiblement]], [[prétendu]])
- Understand the journalistic conditional: [[la Ville envisagerait…]], [[il aurait reçu…]] = unconfirmed
- Name media genres: [[une dépêche]], [[un éditorial]], [[une chronique]], and rewrite a biased text neutrally
